text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Australian Anglican Minister FRANK BETHUNE, who became known as "The Fighting Padre" during World War One, was born in 1877.
Australian pioneer cinecameraman TASMAN HIGGINS, who shot ERROL FLYNN's first film "In The Wake Of The Bounty", was born in 1888.
Canadian actress MARY PICKFORD, who became known as 'America's Sweetheart', was born in 1893.
Australian composer/conductor JOHN ANTILL, whose "G'day Digger" was the first ballet to be televised in Australia, was born in 1904. He was awarded an O.B.E in 1971, and died in January 1987.
Australian construction magnate SIR LESLIE CHARLES THIESS was born in 1909.
Rhodesian Prime Minister IAN SMITH, who declared independence from Britain in 1965, was born in 1919.
British stage and screen actress DOROTHY TUTIN ("The Importance Of Being Earnest") was born in 1930.

British pop musician and son of JOHN LENNON, JULIAN LENNON was born in 1963. His first records appeared in 1984. They included "Too Late For Goodbyes" (1984) and "Valotte" (1984). His recording debut was on his father's recording of "Ya Ya". JULIAN was 11 and he played the drums.
** EVENTS **
1513 : Spanish explorer JUAN PONCE DE LEON discovered
Florida, naming what he thought was an Island after Pascua Florida (Easter Day), the day when the land was first sighted.
1652 : A settlement was founded at the Cape of Good Hope
in Southern Africa, with Dutch East India Company commander JAN VAN RIEBEECK ordering 50-lashes for any of his men caught ill-treating the native Africans in any way.
1817 : A group of Sydney merchants were directed by

GOVERNOR MACQUARIE to set up the 'Bank of New South Wales' in the house of successful businesswoman MARY REIBY. The Bank opened branches in Brisbane in 1850 and Melbourne in 1851, changing its name to 'Westpac' in 1982.
1826 : The first street oil-lamp was lit in Australia, in
Macquarie Street, Sydney.
1907 : Wireless was used for the first time at sea in
Australian waters, when the German ship 'Bremen' sent a radio message announcing its estimated time of arrival in Sydney.
1925 : The Australian Government and the British Colonial
Office offered low-interest loans to encourage half a million Britons to emigrate to Australia.
1941 : Due to the second World War the importation of
luxury items such as canned salmon was restricted.
1950 : Russian ballet dancer VASLAV NIJINSKI died at the
age of 60.
1962 : Cuban leader FIDEL CASTRO offered to ransom
prisoners, held since the invasion of the Bay of Pigs on April 19th, 1961.
1964 : The Moonie-Brisbane oil pipeline was opened.
1966 : United Kingdom figures showed that the number of
illegitimate births in England and Wales had almost doubled in the past ten years.
1973 : Spannish painter PABLO PICASSO died of a heart
attack at the age of 91. His abstract style was born through artistic adventure, and in this form he painted about 140-thousand pieces.
1977 : The punk rock band 'The Damned' became the first
such group to stage a concert in the United States (New York).
1986 : American movie star CLINT EASTWOOD won a landslide
victory to become Mayor of the Californian resort of Carmel.
1989 : More than 40 people died when fire broke out
aboard a Soviet "Mike" class nuclear-submarine, which had refused assistance from nearby merchant ships.
1990 : British golfer NICK FALDO won his second
successive U.S Masters Golf title.
